sentences.en: Hello everyone and I hope you had a wonderful Christmas.
sentences.zh: 大家好，希望你们度过了一个美好的圣诞节。

sentences.en: Now we have two festive treats coming up for you today and on Thursday.
sentences.zh: 今天和周四，我们将为大家带来两份节日大礼。

sentences.en: And these are two halves of a show that we recorded at the Royal Albert Hall on the 4th of May this year with a full orchestra and professional opera singers.
sentences.zh: 这是我们今年 5 月 4 日在皇家阿尔伯特音乐厅录制的一场演出的上下两部分，现场有完整的管弦乐队和专业的歌剧演员助阵。

sentences.en: And it has to be said, me.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有我。

sentences.en: So, like last year's episodes on Mozart and Beethoven, these episodes will be accompanied with music.
sentences.zh: 就像去年关于莫扎特和贝多芬的节目一样，这些剧集也将伴随着音乐。

sentences.en: The first episode, today's episode, is on Tchaikovsky.
sentences.zh: 第一集，也就是今天这一集，主题是柴可夫斯基。

sentences.en: And Thursday's episode will be on Wagner.
sentences.zh: 周四的那一集将讲述瓦格纳。

sentences.en: Enjoy.
sentences.zh: 敬请欣赏。

sentences.en: Welcome or welcome back to The Rest History Live with the Orchestra.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收看《历史的余味》管弦乐现场版。

sentences.en: We have the amazing Philharmonia Orchestra here with us.
sentences.zh: 我们邀请到了出色的爱乐乐团来到现场。

sentences.en: And today we're playing probably my two favourite composers, Tchaikovsky and Wagner.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要演奏的可能是我最喜欢的两位作曲家：柴可夫斯基和瓦格纳的作品。

sentences.en: So, here to tell you more about them are Tom Holland and Dominic Sandbrook.
sentences.zh: 现在，有请汤姆·霍兰德和多米尼克·桑德布鲁克为大家详细介绍他们。

sentences.en: Kensington Gore.
sentences.zh: 肯辛顿戈尔。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到《历史的余味》。

sentences.en: Dominic, it's fantastic to be back at the Royal Albert Hall, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，回到皇家阿尔伯特音乐厅真是太棒了，不是吗？

sentences.en: And thank you so much, everyone, for coming.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家的到来。

sentences.en: And wow, do we have a show this evening.
sentences.zh: 哇，今晚的演出真是精彩绝伦。

sentences.en: We do indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, we will be talking about not just two of Oliver's favourite composers, but two of the greatest composers who have ever lived.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅要谈论奥利弗最喜欢的两位作曲家，还要谈论历史上最伟大的两位作曲家。

sentences.en: Their lives, a brilliant window into the surging passions of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 他们的人生，是洞察 19 世纪澎湃激情的一扇绝佳窗口。

sentences.en: So, we'll be in Russia, under the Tsars.
sentences.zh: 我们将置身于沙皇统治下的俄罗斯。

sentences.en: We'll be in Germany, in the age of Bismarck.
sentences.zh: 我们将置身于俾斯麦时代的德国。

sentences.en: A world of romantic idealism, of sexual secrets, of Tom.
sentences.zh: 那是一个充满浪漫理想主义、性秘密和汤姆的世界。

sentences.en: Some very pungent politics.
sentences.zh: 还有一些非常辛辣的政治话题。

sentences.en: Very pungent.
sentences.zh: 非常辛辣。

sentences.en: We do like pungent politics, and the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 我们确实喜欢辛辣的政治，而剩下的就是历史了。

sentences.en: This show really does have it all.
sentences.zh: 这场演出真的是应有尽有。

sentences.en: It really does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And you've already had a flavour of the music we're going to be hearing this evening.
sentences.zh: 大家刚才已经领略了我们今晚将要欣赏到的音乐风格。

sentences.en: So, that, of course, was the opening of Tchaikovsky's ballet, Swan Lake.
sentences.zh: 那当然就是柴可夫斯基芭蕾舞剧《天鹅湖》的开场曲。

sentences.en: First performed in 1877, and, as Ollie said, played by the Philharmonia Orchestra and conducted by the equally brilliant Oliver Zethman.
sentences.zh: 该剧首演于 1877 年，正如奥利所说，由爱乐乐团演奏，并由同样出色的奥利弗·泽特曼指挥。

sentences.en: And we should start by paying tribute to Oliver, because these shows were his idea.
sentences.zh: 我们首先要向奥利弗致敬，因为这些演出都是他的主意。

sentences.en: He literally put the band together.
sentences.zh: 是他一手组建了这支乐队。

sentences.en: And, as you will find out, and as you've already discovered with that wonderful performance of Swan Lake, he's not half bad at conducting, either.
sentences.zh: 正如你们即将发现的，也正如你们刚才从那段精彩的《天鹅湖》表演中所感受到的，他的指挥水平也相当不错。

sentences.en: Not bad at all.
sentences.zh: 相当不错。

sentences.en: But let's get right into our first story.
sentences.zh: 但让我们直接进入第一个故事吧。

sentences.en: And this is the life of perhaps the most romantic, and certainly the most flamboyantly Russian, of all the great composers.
sentences.zh: 这将讲述也许是所有伟大作曲家中最浪漫、当然也是最具俄罗斯风情的一位的人生。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: So, this whole show that we have for you this evening is very much a 19th century affair, and we're going to kick off in the year 1840,
sentences.zh: 今晚我们为大家呈现的整场演出都带有浓厚的 19 世纪色彩，我们将从 1840 年开始讲起，

sentences.en: because that is the year that a young Piotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky was born in a little iron-making town called Votshinsk,
sentences.zh: 因为那一年，年轻的彼得·伊里奇·柴可夫斯基出生在沃特金斯克一个小小的炼铁镇，
zh_words: 彼得·伊里奇·柴可夫斯基

sentences.en: which is about 600 miles east of Moscow, in the foothills of the Urals.
sentences.zh: 那里位于莫斯科以东约 600 英里处，在乌拉尔山脉的山脚下。

sentences.en: So, we are deep in the heart of Russia.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们正深入俄罗斯的心脏地带。

sentences.en: We're in a classic Russian landscape.
sentences.zh: 我们置身于经典的俄罗斯风景之中。

sentences.en: They're kind of churches with their golden domes, the vast fields, the deep birch and beech forests.
sentences.zh: 那里有金顶教堂、广袤的田野，以及深邃的桦树和山毛榉森林。

sentences.en: It's the kind of landscape that is familiar if you've read Tolstoy or Dostoevsky or any of the great Russian novelists, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 如果你读过托尔斯泰、陀思妥耶夫斯基或任何一位俄罗斯伟大作家的小说，这种风景应该很熟悉，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: So, to give you a bit of context,
sentences.zh: 为了给大家一点背景介绍，

sentences.en: Russia at the time is an autocracy ruled by the Romanov czars.
sentences.zh: 当时的俄罗斯是一个由罗曼诺夫王朝沙皇统治的专制国家。

sentences.en: And it's got this vast population of serfs and peasants.
sentences.zh: 它拥有庞大的农奴和农民人口。

sentences.en: Now, it's often described as a backward country, but that's not necessarily true in every respect.
sentences.zh: 虽然它常被描述为一个落后的国家，但这并不完全属实。

sentences.en: Russia has been expanding at a colossal rate by 1840 when Tchaikovsky is born.
sentences.zh: 到 1840 年柴可夫斯基出生时，俄罗斯一直在以惊人的速度扩张。

sentences.en: It's a vast continental empire, all the way from Finland and Poland to the Caucasus and the Pacific.
sentences.zh: 它是一个横跨芬兰、波兰，一直延伸到高加索和太平洋的庞大大陆帝国。

sentences.en: And Tchaikovsky's family is doing well out of the Russian empire, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 柴可夫斯基的家庭在俄罗斯帝国过得不错，对吧？

sentences.en: So, his father manages the local ironworks.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲负责管理当地的铁厂。

sentences.en: They've got servants.
sentences.zh: 他们家里有仆人。

sentences.en: And actually, shocking detail, Dominic,
sentences.zh: 而且，多米尼克，有一个令人震惊的细节，

sentences.en: Tchaikovsky's mother's family are actually French.
sentences.zh: 柴可夫斯基母亲的家族其实是法国人。

sentences.en: They are Huguenots who fled to Russia as refugees.
sentences.zh: 他们是作为难民逃到俄罗斯的胡格诺教徒。

sentences.en: So, we're not holding that against them.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们不会因此而对他们有偏见。

sentences.en: No, we don't hold that against them.
sentences.zh: 不，我们不会因此而对他们有偏见。

sentences.en: So, he even actually had a French governess.
sentences.zh: 他甚至还有一位法国女家庭教师。

sentences.en: And we know a few details about Tchaikovsky's early life from the French governess.
sentences.zh: 我们从这位法国女教师那里了解到了一些关于柴可夫斯基早年生活的细节。

sentences.en: She said he was a bright boy, but incredibly sensitive.
sentences.zh: 她说他是个聪明的孩子，但极其敏感。

sentences.en: She said he was as brittle as porcelain, a child of glass.
sentences.zh: 她说他像瓷器一样脆弱，是个玻璃做的孩子。

sentences.en: And Tom, very much like our goal-hanger stablemates.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这很像我们《Goalhanger》的同事们。

sentences.en: We actually have Rory Stewart with us in the audience.
sentences.zh: 我们观众席里其实坐着罗里·斯图尔特。

sentences.en: And nobody would ever say Rory was as brittle as porcelain.
sentences.zh: 没人会说罗里像瓷器一样脆弱。

sentences.en: Of course not.
sentences.zh: 当然不会。

sentences.en: Of course not.
sentences.zh: 当然不会。

sentences.en: So, the Tchaikovsky's, they're not a tremendously musical family, actually, as it happens.
sentences.zh: 柴可夫斯基一家其实并不是一个特别有音乐氛围的家庭。

sentences.en: I mean, they do have a piano, but basically everyone who's middle class in the 19th century has a piano.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们确实有一架钢琴，但 19 世纪的中产阶级基本上家家都有钢琴。

sentences.en: And none of them are very good at playing it.
sentences.zh: 而且他们谁弹得都不怎么样。

sentences.en: No, they're not terribly good at it.
sentences.zh: 不，他们弹得确实不怎么样。

sentences.en: But then one day, Piotr's father, Ilya, comes home from St. Petersburg.
sentences.zh: 但有一天，彼得的父亲伊利亚从圣彼得堡出差回来。

sentences.en: He's been on a business trip.
sentences.zh: 他带回了一种叫“管弦乐器”的自动风琴。

sentences.en: And he has this kind of barrel organ called an orchestrion.
sentences.zh: 这种机器的意义在于，它基本上能模拟整个管弦乐队的声音。

sentences.en: And the point of this machine is that it would basically mimic the sound of an entire orchestra.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们能投资买一台那个，其实就不需要爱乐乐团了。

sentences.en: So, we wouldn't actually need the Philharmonia if we could only invest it in one of those.
sentences.zh: 奥利弗的生活会轻松得多。

sentences.en: Oliver's life would be so much easier.
sentences.zh: 这就是年轻的柴可夫斯基爱上音乐的方式。

sentences.en: So, this is how the young Tchaikovsky falls in love with music.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你把乐谱塞进这个东西里，然后转动它。

sentences.en: Basically, you feed a sheet into this thing and you turn it.
sentences.zh: 它可以是莫扎特的金曲精选。

sentences.en: It could be, you know, Mozart's greatest hits.
sentences.zh: 然后就开始演奏了。

sentences.en: And away you go.
sentences.zh: 事实上，柴可夫斯基真正爱上的是莫扎特。

sentences.en: And actually, it's Mozart that Tchaikovsky really falls in love with.
sentences.zh: 莫扎特成了他伟大的偶像。

sentences.en: Mozart becomes his great hero.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几年里，他们一家搬迁了好几次。

sentences.en: So, in the next few years, the family move around quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 他们见识了圣彼得堡和莫斯科这些城市。

sentences.en: Sort of, they see the cities, St. Petersburg and Moscow.
sentences.zh: 他们去了乌拉尔山脉的不同地方。

sentences.en: They go to different places in the Urals.
sentences.zh: 我常想，这种频繁搬迁的经历是否赋予了柴可夫斯基

sentences.en: And I often wonder whether this is, the fact that they move around, whether this gives Tchaikovsky
sentences.zh: 他最显著的特征之一，那就是对俄罗斯人民和土地有着非凡的亲和力。

sentences.en: one of his defining traits, which is an extraordinary affinity with the people and landscape of Russia.
sentences.zh: 那种强烈的爱国情怀。

sentences.en: This intense sense of patriotism.
sentences.zh: 晚年时他曾写道：我从未见过比我更热爱俄罗斯母亲的人。

sentences.en: Much later on in life, he wrote, I have never come across anyone more in love with Mother Russia than me.
sentences.zh: 我热爱俄罗斯人民、俄罗斯语言、俄罗斯的思维方式。

sentences.en: I love Russian people, the Russian language, the Russian way of thinking.
sentences.zh: 我热爱那朦胧而遥远的过去的神圣传说。

sentences.en: I love the sacred legends of the dim and distant paSt.
sentences.zh: 我热爱这一切。

sentences.en: I love it all.
sentences.zh: 但矛盾的是，尽管它非常俄罗斯，但它同时也非常欧洲，不是吗？

sentences.en: But, I mean, almost the paradox of this is that even as it's very Russian, it's also very European, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为欧洲文化仍然深受浪漫主义、风景崇拜和感性崇拜的影响。

sentences.en: Because European culture is still very marked by romanticism, by the cult of landscape, the cult of sensibility.
sentences.zh: 我想最重要的是，民族主义的崇拜。

sentences.en: And I guess above all, the cult of nationalism.
sentences.zh: 所以，整个欧洲的各类作家和作曲家，不仅仅是在俄罗斯，都对民间传统、历史以及古老的神话传说着迷。

sentences.en: So, all sorts of writers and composers across Europe, not just in Russia, are fascinated by folk traditions and history and ancient myths and legends.
sentences.zh: 在下半场，我们将提到另一位对神话传说感兴趣的人。

sentences.en: And we will be coming on to someone else who is interested in myths and legends in the second half.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: We will indeed.
sentences.zh: 但在他成长的过程中，我想对于他的家人来说，

sentences.en: But at the time when he was growing up, I think to his family,
sentences.zh: 柴可夫斯基会成为承载这一切的伟大俄罗斯音乐载体，这在当时看来是相对不可想象的。

sentences.en: the idea that Tchaikovsky would be the great Russian musical vehicle for all this would have seemed relatively unthinkable.
sentences.zh: 因为虽然他们有钢琴，正如你所说，大多数俄罗斯中产阶级家庭都有钢琴。

sentences.en: Because although they have a piano, you know, most Russians, as you said, have a piano, most Russian middle class families.
sentences.zh: 但在俄罗斯，中产阶级男孩是不会去当音乐家的。

sentences.en: But in Russia, middle class boys don't go on to become musicians.
sentences.zh: 所以当他们去歌剧院或音乐厅时，听到的都是来巡演的西欧音乐家。

sentences.en: So when they go to the opera house or the concert hall, the musicians they hear playing are touring Western European musicians.
sentences.zh: 这在当时看来，并不是像柴可夫斯基这样的人该做的事。

sentences.en: It's not seen as a proper thing for someone like Tchaikovsky to do.
sentences.zh: 因此，起初柴可夫斯基并没有追求音乐事业。

sentences.en: So, to begin with, Tchaikovsky doesn't pursue a musical career.
sentences.zh: 他追求的是一个更光鲜的职业，那就是成为一名公务员。

sentences.en: He pursues a much more glamorous profession, which is to become a civil servant.
sentences.zh: 我这么说绝非开玩笑，因为读过俄罗斯小说的人都知道，成为一名公务员确实非同小可。

sentences.en: And I'm not joking when I say that, because, I mean, anyone who's read a Russian novel will know that to be a civil servant is really quite something.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常令人向往的职业，而且很难进入。

sentences.en: Very prestigious vacation, very difficult to get into.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实很难进入。

sentences.en: Right, it is difficult to get into.
sentences.zh: 所以在他 12 岁时，父母把他送到了圣彼得堡的一所寄宿学校，名叫法律学校。

sentences.en: So when he's 12 years old, his parents sent him to a boarding school in St. Petersburg, which is called the School of Jurisprudence.
sentences.zh: 那是学习成为官员的地方。

sentences.en: That's where you learn to become an official.
sentences.zh: 所以他穿着军装。

sentences.en: So he wears a military uniform.
sentences.zh: 他在 12 岁时就必须向上帝、王位和祖国宣誓。

sentences.en: He has to swear an oath at the age of 12 to God, throne and motherland.
sentences.zh: 他每天必须从早上 6 点工作到晚上 10 点。

sentences.en: And he has to work every day from 6 o'clock in the morning until 10 o'clock at night.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这就是我们让自己的制片人西奥和塔比复制的作息时间。

sentences.en: And that is the routine, Tom, that we have replicated with our own producers, Theo and Tabby.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我觉得你是在恭维西奥，他从来没在中午之前起过床。

sentences.en: I think, Dominic, you are flattering Theo there, who is never knowingly up before midday.
sentences.zh: 不，你说得对，你说得对。

sentences.en: No, you're right, you're right.
sentences.zh: 你能这么说真是太好了。

sentences.en: It's sweet of you to say that.
sentences.zh: 柴可夫斯基在那所学校一直待到 19 岁，之后他成为了司法部的一名行政助理。

sentences.en: So Tchaikovsky is there in this school until he's 19, and then he becomes an administrative assistant at the Ministry of Justice.
sentences.zh: 但在这期间，他一直沉迷于音乐。

sentences.en: But all this time he's been into his music.
sentences.zh: 他一直在写华尔兹、歌曲之类的东西。

sentences.en: He's been writing waltzes and songs and things.

sentences.zh: 后来在1832年，另一位沙皇尼古拉一世宣布，任何被判有同性恋行为的平民都将被流放到西伯利亚。

sentences.zh: 说实话，这似乎是俄罗斯沙皇对几乎任何事情的反应。

sentences.en: But most of these punishments were never carried out.
sentences.zh: 但这些惩罚大多从未真正执行过。

sentences.en: And I think that's because in 19th century Russia, homosexuality, it didn't kind of define you.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是因为在19世纪的俄罗斯，同性恋并不会定义你。

sentences.zh: 所以，如果你有钱，有关系，被起诉甚至定罪的可能性其实非常非常小，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 正如你所说，同性恋被东正教谴责为一种恶习。

sentences.en: But it's fascinating that in all Tchaikovsky's life, there is only one tiny hint of scandal or public criticism.
sentences.zh: 但令人着迷的是，在柴可夫斯基的一生中，只有一次微小的丑闻或公众批评的迹象。

sentences.en: And that's a newspaper article in 1878 that was sort of muttering darkly about the teachers' love affairs at the Moscow Conservatory.

sentences.en: But that hasn't stopped Tchaikovsky's biographers since from kind of basically tearing each other to shreds over the question of whether he felt haunted by his sexuality or whether he was completely mellow about it.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有阻止柴可夫斯基的传记作者们为了他是否被自己的性取向所困扰，还是对此完全泰然处之的问题而争论不休。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, in the Soviet Union, this was a big problem for historians and biographers of Tchaikovsky.
sentences.zh: 在苏联，这对柴可夫斯基的历史学家和传记作者来说是个大问题。

sentences.en: And they went out of their way to play down his sexuality.
sentences.zh: 他们竭尽全力淡化他的性取向。

sentences.zh: 事实上，苏联历史学家甚至进入档案馆删除了他们认为对他形象不利的材料。

sentences.en: But in the West, particularly, I have to say, in Britain, people tended to play it up.

sentences.zh: 所以，在20世纪的西方学术界，柴可夫斯基被视为“那个同性恋作曲家”。

sentences.en: So, first of all, kind of condemned as a hysterical neurotic, and then held up as a hero of gay rights.

sentences.en: But, I mean, not saying that he's a hysterical neurotic, but there are hints that he struggled with his sexuality, aren't there?

sentences.en: So, I mean, he's kind of the Russian Oscar Wilde, maybe, in that sense.

sentences.en: So, kind of a great gay icon.

sentences.en: And Taruskin said, look, we should stop seeing Tchaikovsky as this angst-ridden, guilt-ridden kind of neurotic artiSt.
sentences.zh: 塔鲁斯金说，看，我们应该停止把柴可夫斯基看作那种充满焦虑、充满内疚的神经质艺术家。

sentences.en: By and large, this is somebody who is very successful, who has loads of fun, actually loads of money, and is generally pretty happy.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，这是一个非常成功的人，他有很多乐趣，实际上有很多钱，而且总体上相当快乐。

sentences.en: All of that said, Tom, you are right that there are issues, shall we say, because in 1876, he does basically the most unexpected and implausible thing you could possibly imagine.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，汤姆，你说得对，确实存在一些问题，因为在1876年，他确实做了你能想象到的最出人意料、最不可思议的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, so unexpected, so implausible, that I think we should probably have a bit of music beforehand to brace ourselves for it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，太出人意料，太不可思议了，我想我们应该先听点音乐来做好心理准备。

sentences.en: And what we're going to hear now is a piece he wrote in 1878 amid the great emotional crisis of, spoiler alert, Tchaikovsky's marriage.
sentences.zh: 我们现在要听的是他1878年在剧透预警——柴可夫斯基婚姻的巨大情感危机中创作的一首曲子。

sentences.en: So, Dominic.

sentences.en: Tchaikovsky's marriage.
sentences.zh: 柴可夫斯基的婚姻。

sentences.en: I think we've established he's very much not the marrying kind of a guy.
sentences.zh: 我想我们已经确定他根本不是那种会结婚的人。

sentences.en: So, what's going on there?
sentences.zh: 那么，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: I mean, does he think it's his duty?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他觉得这是他的责任吗？

sentences.en: He's got to lie back and think of Russia?
sentences.zh: 他得躺平了去想俄罗斯的事？

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Tchaikovsky felt the pressure of social expectation, basically.
sentences.zh: 柴可夫斯基基本上是感受到了社会期望的压力。

sentences.en: I think he felt that he ought to get married, that it was the thing to do, whether he wanted to or not.
sentences.zh: 我想他觉得他应该结婚，觉得这是必须做的事，不管他想不想。

sentences.en: So, already in 1868, he had proposed to a soprano called Desire Artaud, which I think is a sensational name for a soprano.
sentences.zh: 所以，早在 1868 年，他就向一位名叫德西蕾·阿托的歌剧女高音求婚了，我觉得这对于女高音来说是个非常轰动的名字。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And she says yes.
sentences.zh: 而她答应了。

sentences.en: Yes, she did, but it very quickly, I think much to his relief, fizzled out and she married somebody else.
sentences.zh: 是的，她答应了，但我想让他感到宽慰的是，这段关系很快就无疾而终了，她嫁给了别人。

sentences.en: But then, in 1877, he started getting letters from a young woman called Antonina Miljakova.
sentences.zh: 但后来，在 1877 年，他开始收到一位名叫安东尼娜·米利亚科娃的年轻女性的来信。

sentences.en: And she had very briefly been a student of his, a music student.
sentences.zh: 她曾短暂地做过他的学生，一名音乐系学生。

sentences.en: Now, Tchaikovsky had completely forgotten her, but she had certainly not forgotten him.
sentences.zh: 现在，柴可夫斯基已经完全忘记了她，但她肯定没有忘记他。

sentences.en: She had developed this great crush on Tchaikovsky.
sentences.zh: 她对柴可夫斯基产生了极大的迷恋。

sentences.en: And she basically starts sending him these letters.
sentences.zh: 她基本上开始给他写这些信。

sentences.en: She's a super fan, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想她是个超级粉丝。

sentences.en: And he agrees to meet her.
sentences.zh: 他同意去见她。

sentences.en: And at the second meeting, I think very recklessly, he asks her to marry him.
sentences.zh: 在第二次见面时，我想他非常鲁莽地向她求婚了。

sentences.en: And immediately she says, oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 她立刻就说，哦，好的。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: And Tchaikovsky thinks, I have made a huge mistake.
sentences.zh: 而柴可夫斯基心想，我犯了一个大错。

sentences.en: And so, the wedding, when it happens, is not 100% the kind of wedding that a bride dreams of, is it?
sentences.zh: 所以，当婚礼举行时，那并不是新娘梦寐以求的那种婚礼，对吧？

sentences.en: Because they get married in Moscow in July 1877.
sentences.zh: 因为他们于 1877 年 7 月在莫斯科结婚。

sentences.en: And when the priest says to Tchaikovsky, you may kiss the bride, Tchaikovsky responds by bursting into tears.
sentences.zh: 当牧师对柴可夫斯基说“你可以亲吻新娘”时，柴可夫斯基的反应是泪流满面。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the wedding night's not a bundle of laughs either.
sentences.zh: 是啊，所以新婚之夜也没什么好笑的。

sentences.en: Because as soon as they reach the hotel, Tchaikovsky, in sort of desperation, takes a massive sedative and goes straight to sleep.
sentences.zh: 因为他们一到酒店，柴可夫斯基出于绝望，就服用了一大剂镇静剂，直接睡着了。

sentences.en: And poor Antonina has no idea what's going on.
sentences.zh: 可怜的安东尼娜根本不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: But it's fair to say nothing much is going on.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定地说，什么都没发生。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because a few days later, Tchaikovsky writes to his brother and he says, look, I find my wife absolutely repulsive.
sentences.zh: 因为几天后，柴可夫斯基写信给他的兄弟说，看，我觉得我的妻子简直令人作呕。

sentences.en: And Tchaikovsky capable of great charm, but not on this occasion.
sentences.zh: 柴可夫斯基虽然很有魅力，但这次却并非如此。

sentences.en: No, not on this occasion.
sentences.zh: 不，这次不是。

sentences.en: So, he's very miserable.
sentences.zh: 所以，他非常痛苦。

sentences.en: He's made a terrible mistake.
sentences.zh: 他犯了一个可怕的错误。

sentences.en: He thinks about throwing himself into the river Moskva.
sentences.zh: 他想过投莫斯科河自尽。

sentences.en: But in the end, he basically flees to the countryside and leaves Antonina behind.
sentences.zh: 但最终，他基本上逃到了乡下，把安东尼娜留在了身后。

sentences.en: And not just the countryside, right?
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是乡下，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, he basically goes on a massive European holiday.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他基本上去了一场大规模的欧洲度假。

sentences.en: So, he goes to Paris, to Florence, to Rome, to Vienna, desperately trying to think of ways to avoid her.
sentences.zh: 所以，他去了巴黎、佛罗伦萨、罗马、维也纳，拼命想办法躲着她。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then in the middle of all this, I mean, it should really have been his honeymoon.
sentences.zh: 而在这一切之中，我是说，这本该是他的蜜月。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And his great love interest, Josef Kotec, pitches up in Switzerland to see him, which I imagine doesn't help with his kind of,
sentences.zh: 而他深爱的人，约瑟夫·科特克，跑到了瑞士去见他，我想这对他那种“我真的应该回到妻子身边”的想法没什么帮助。

sentences.en: I should really get back with my wife kind of thoughts.
sentences.zh: 我真的应该回到妻子身边，他心里是这么想的。

sentences.en: So, you may remember from a few moments earlier that we said Kotec was a violiniSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可能还记得刚才我们说过科特克是一位小提琴家。

sentences.en: So, this is actually the moment that inspires Tchaikovsky to write the piece that we have just heard, the Violin Concerto.
sentences.zh: 所以，这实际上就是激发柴可夫斯基创作我们刚刚听到的那部作品——《小提琴协奏曲》的时刻。

sentences.en: And when you listen to it, you can feel there's this kind of incredible sense of excitement.
sentences.zh: 当你听它的时候，你能感觉到那种难以置信的兴奋感。

sentences.en: So, I mean, musicologists must hate this kind of talk, but perhaps there's a sense there of the frenzy of passion that he's feeling for Kotec.
sentences.zh: 所以，我是说，音乐学家一定很讨厌这种说法，但也许其中有一种他为科特克感受到的那种疯狂激情的意味。

sentences.en: But also, it's a little bit mad, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这也有一点疯狂，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And maybe that's the effects of his marriage.
sentences.zh: 也许这就是他婚姻的影响。

sentences.en: Well, here's a really mad thing.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这里有一件真正疯狂的事。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: the mad thing is that that piece that we've just heard played so brilliantly got one of the worst reviews in the history of classical music from the great Viennese critic of the day,
sentences.zh: 疯狂的是，我们刚刚听到的那部演奏得如此精彩的作品，却遭到了当时维也纳伟大评论家爱德华·汉斯利克在古典音乐史上最糟糕的评价之一。

sentences.en: Edouard Hanslick.
sentences.zh: 爱德华·汉斯利克。

sentences.en: Hanslick said that listening to that was like being in hell.
sentences.zh: 汉斯利克说听那部作品就像身处地狱。

sentences.en: He said, Tchaikovsky has proved for the first time the hideous notion that there can be music that stinks to the ear.
sentences.zh: 他说，柴可夫斯基第一次证明了那个可怕的观点，即世界上可能存在听起来令人作呕的音乐。

sentences.en: I mean, that is mad.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, Tom, as we often tell rival podcasters, rival history podcasters, you should never let the critics get you down.
sentences.zh: 好吧，汤姆，正如我们经常告诉竞争对手播客，那些历史类播客同行一样，你永远不应该让评论家让你消沉。

sentences.en: So true.
sentences.zh: 太对了。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, just two questions.
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，就两个问题。

sentences.en: And I'm guessing the answer to both of these questions is no.
sentences.zh: 我猜这两个问题的答案都是“不”。

sentences.en: Did they ever consummate their relationship?
sentences.zh: 他们圆房了吗？

sentences.en: They did not.
sentences.zh: 他们没有。

sentences.en: And did they ever get back together?
sentences.zh: 他们复合了吗？

sentences.en: Again, they did not.
sentences.zh: 同样，他们没有。

sentences.en: So, he went back to Russia.
sentences.zh: 所以，他回到了俄罗斯。

sentences.en: He asked Antonina for a divorce.
sentences.zh: 他向安东尼娜提出了离婚。

sentences.en: She said no.
sentences.zh: 她说不。

sentences.en: They separated, but they didn't divorce.
sentences.zh: 他们分居了，但没有离婚。

sentences.en: He did give her financial help later in life.
sentences.zh: 他后来确实在经济上帮助过她。

sentences.en: And they did sometimes meet, but he was always, I have to say, very cold and almost a little bit cruel when they met.
sentences.zh: 他们有时也会见面，但我不得不说，当他们见面时，他总是非常冷漠，甚至有点残忍。

sentences.en: And actually, by and large, when people talk about the great composers, they always overlook, or indeed are downright rude about, the wives.
sentences.zh: 事实上，总的来说，当人们谈论伟大的作曲家时，他们总是忽视，甚至对他们的妻子非常粗鲁。

sentences.en: So, perhaps we should spare a thought for Antonina.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许我们应该为安东尼娜想一想。

sentences.en: She had a really rough time through no fault of her own.
sentences.zh: 她经历了一段非常艰难的时期，而这并不是她的错。

sentences.en: She actually ended up going mad and ended up in a lunatic asylum.
sentences.zh: 她最终疯了，住进了精神病院。

sentences.en: So, it's a very sad story.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个非常悲伤的故事。

sentences.en: And there's kind of sense that meeting Tchaikovsky isn't always great for your long-term mental stability here, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 而且有一种感觉，遇见柴可夫斯基对你的长期心理稳定来说并不总是好事，不是吗？

sentences.en: And I wonder, Dominic, whether it was worse for Antonina, precisely because she had been such a fan.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，多米尼克，这对安东尼娜来说是不是更糟糕，恰恰因为她曾经是他的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And they separate, just as Tchaikovsky is about to embark on the kind of, you know, the absolute pinnacle of his career, so the 1880s.
sentences.zh: 他们分居了，就在柴可夫斯基即将开启他职业生涯巅峰的时候，也就是 1880 年代。

sentences.en: He's become a massive national, actually an international celebrity, and people are comparing him to Mozart and saying that he can turn his hand to anything.
sentences.zh: 他已经成为了一位巨大的民族，实际上是国际名人，人们把他和莫扎特相提并论，说他什么都能做。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, not anything, obviously not marriage, but symphonies, concertos, ballets, you name it, basically Tchaikovsky can do it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我是说，不是什么都能做，显然婚姻不行，但交响曲、协奏曲、芭蕾舞剧，随你怎么说，基本上柴可夫斯基都能搞定。

sentences.en: Very Mozart.
sentences.zh: 非常有莫扎特的风范。

sentences.en: Yeah, and this is not just a question of Tchaikovsky's genius, it's also a question of the context.
sentences.zh: 是的，这不仅仅是柴可夫斯基的天才问题，也是背景问题。

sentences.en: So, in the 1880s, I mean, Russia obviously has some pretty, pretty major political issues which culminate in the Russian Revolution, but culturally,
sentences.zh: 所以，在 1880 年代，俄罗斯显然有一些非常、非常重大的政治问题，最终导致了俄国革命，但在文化上，

sentences.en: it's a very rich and self-confident and sophisticated place.
sentences.zh: 它是一个非常丰富、自信和成熟的地方。

sentences.en: Now, the Tsar at the time, Alexander III, is a massive reactionary, and he is very keen on the idea that Russia is distinct from the rest of Europe,
sentences.zh: 当时沙皇亚历山大三世是一个巨大的反动派，他非常热衷于俄罗斯有别于欧洲其他国家的想法，

sentences.en: that it's sort of set apart by its Slavic history and identity.
sentences.zh: 认为它因其斯拉夫历史和身份而与众不同。

sentences.en: And so, for Alexander and his court, the idea that Tchaikovsky is a distinctly Russian composer with a distinct Russian style,
sentences.zh: 因此，对于亚历山大和他的宫廷来说，柴可夫斯基是一位具有独特俄罗斯风格的俄罗斯作曲家，

sentences.en: borrowing from traditional folk melodies and songs and whatnot, that becomes really, really important to them.
sentences.zh: 借鉴了传统的民间旋律和歌曲等等，这对他们来说变得非常、非常重要。

sentences.en: Despite the fact that this is exactly the kind of thing that is going on in countries across Europe, so Sibelius is doing it, Vaughan Williams in New Course will do it.
sentences.zh: 尽管事实上这正是欧洲各国正在发生的事情，西贝柳斯在做，沃恩·威廉斯当然也会做。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, what does the Tsar say to that?
sentences.zh: 那么沙皇对此怎么说？

sentences.en: But the Tsar doesn't give a damn about that, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得可以公平地说，沙皇根本不在乎这些。

sentences.en: So, the Tsar, to the Tsar, he doesn't give a damn what Sibelius is doing, all that matters to him is that Tchaikovsky is a sort of authentic Russian hero.
sentences.zh: 所以，对沙皇来说，他根本不在乎西贝柳斯在做什么，对他来说唯一重要的是柴可夫斯基是一位地道的俄罗斯英雄。

sentences.en: So, in 1884, he invites Tchaikovsky to St. Petersburg to receive the Order of St. Vladimir, an extraordinary honour for a composer.
sentences.zh: 所以，在 1884 年，他邀请柴可夫斯基去圣彼得堡接受圣弗拉基米尔勋章，这对一位作曲家来说是极大的荣誉。

sentences.en: He gives him a ring as a personal present, and he also gives him a lifetime pension, which is a sign of just how much Tchaikovsky is valued.
sentences.zh: 他送给他一枚戒指作为私人礼物，还给了他一份终身养老金，这标志着柴可夫斯基受到了多么高的重视。

sentences.en: So, putting the marriage to one side, his life is pretty good.
sentences.zh: 撇开婚姻不谈，他的生活其实相当不错。

sentences.en: So, he's got his pension, he's got his kind of honour, he's very popular, he's kind of famous, and he even has a kind of very, well, actually, the kind of perfect patron,
sentences.zh: 他有养老金，有某种荣誉，非常受欢迎，也算是个名人，甚至还有一位非常——嗯，实际上是完美的赞助人，

sentences.en: who's a woman called Nadezhda von Meck.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫娜杰日达·冯·梅克的女士。

sentences.en: And she's the perfect patron, because they never meet, but she just chucks loads of money at him.
sentences.zh: 她是完美的赞助人，因为他们从未谋面，但她总是慷慨地资助他。

sentences.en: Right, yes.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实。

sentences.en: And also, he's a massive star in America, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且他在美国也是超级巨星，不是吗？

sentences.en: Right, so he's actually very like us.
sentences.zh: 所以，他其实和我们很像。

sentences.en: He goes to New York in 1890.
sentences.zh: 他在1890年去了纽约。

sentences.en: He conducts at Carnegie Hall.
sentences.zh: 他在卡内基音乐厅担任指挥。

sentences.en: He loves it.
sentences.zh: 他很喜欢那里。

sentences.en: The thing he loved most when he came back, and he couldn't stop talking about it, was the telephone in his hotel.
sentences.zh: 他回来后最喜欢、也最津津乐道的事情，就是他酒店房间里的电话。

sentences.en: He was amazed by this telephone, and he kept ringing in the reception, just to kind of try out the phone.
sentences.zh: 他对这台电话感到惊奇，不停地打给前台，只是为了试用一下电话。

sentences.en: Very like Theo Young-Smith, on our American tours, ringing for room service.
sentences.zh: 这和我们在美国巡演时的西奥·杨-史密斯很像，总是打电话叫客房服务。

sentences.en: He was never off the telephone, was he?
sentences.zh: 他简直离不开电话，对吧？

sentences.en: And then when he gets back home from America, he gets to work on one of the most joyous and celebrated things that he ever wrote, and that is his ballet, The Nutcracker.
sentences.zh: 从美国回到家后，他开始创作他一生中最欢乐、最著名的作品之一，那就是他的芭蕾舞剧《胡桃夹子》。

sentences.en: And the good news, Dominic, ladies and gentlemen, is that we are now going to hear two of its most glorious moments right now.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，各位听众，好消息是，我们现在就要欣赏其中最辉煌的两个片段了。

sentences.en: The sad news is that we are not going to dance to it, but you can't have everything.
sentences.zh: 坏消息是我们不能跟着跳舞，但鱼和熊掌不可兼得嘛。

sentences.en: That, of course, was the dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy, and the Russian dance, both from The Nutcracker and Dominic.
sentences.zh: 刚才那段当然是《胡桃夹子》里的《糖果仙子之舞》和《俄罗斯舞曲》，多米尼克。

sentences.en: It's starting to feel a lot like Christmas, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 感觉很有圣诞气氛了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because, of course, The Nutcracker, the story of a wooden Nutcracker doll that comes to life at Christmas.
sentences.zh: 因为《胡桃夹子》讲的当然是一个木制胡桃夹子玩偶在圣诞节复活的故事。

sentences.en: Yes, and that was first performed in St. Petersburg in December 1892.
sentences.zh: 是的，它于1892年12月在圣彼得堡首演。

sentences.en: So, at the time, Tchaikovsky was 52 years old, he was at the peak of his powers, the peak of his popularity, and he's probably got, what, 20 years ahead of him,
sentences.zh: 当时柴可夫斯基52岁，正处于创作生涯和人气巅峰，他大概还有，嗯，20年的时间，

sentences.en: writing unimaginable masterpieces.
sentences.zh: 去创作那些不可思议的杰作。

sentences.en: But just a year later, his story takes a tragic twiSt.
sentences.zh: 但仅仅一年后，他的故事发生了悲剧性的转折。

sentences.en: So, on the 10th of October, 1893, Tchaikovsky arrives in St. Petersburg by train, and he's planning to stay with his younger brother, who we've already mentioned, Modeste.
sentences.zh: 1893年10月10日，柴可夫斯基乘火车抵达圣彼得堡，计划住在我们之前提到过的弟弟莫杰斯特家里。

sentences.en: And, Dominic, we're going to be talking about the history of St. Petersburg in a couple of weeks on the podcast, because, of course, we're doing Peter the Great,
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我们几周后会在播客里讨论圣彼得堡的历史，因为我们当然要讲彼得大帝，

sentences.en: and St. Petersburg is founded by Peter the Great on very marshy, very boggy land, a lot of mosquitoes, and so it is notoriously unhealthy, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 圣彼得堡是彼得大帝在沼泽地带建立的，蚊子很多，所以众所周知那里很不健康，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's always been plagued by cholera outbreaks, one of which is raging in the autumn of 1893.
sentences.zh: 那里一直饱受霍乱爆发的困扰，1893年秋天正值疫情肆虐。

sentences.en: And all the restaurants have been told by the authorities that they have to boil their water before giving it to the customers.
sentences.zh: 当局已经通知所有餐馆，必须将水煮沸后才能提供给顾客。

sentences.en: But 10 days into his stay, the 20th of October, Tchaikovsky goes out with his mates on the Nevsky Prospect, and they go into a restaurant, and he asks for water.
sentences.zh: 但在他入住的第10天，也就是10月20日，柴可夫斯基和朋友们去涅瓦大街逛街，他们走进一家餐馆，他要了杯水。

sentences.en: And the waiter says, we've just run out of all the boiled water.
sentences.zh: 服务员说，我们刚用完了所有的开水。

sentences.en: If you hold on a little while, we'll get you some more.
sentences.zh: 如果您稍等片刻，我们再去给您烧一些。

sentences.en: Tchaikovsky says, I don't want to wait.
sentences.zh: 柴可夫斯基说，我不想等。

sentences.en: I'm very thirsty.
sentences.zh: 我太渴了。

sentences.en: I'm sure it's fine.
sentences.zh: 我相信没问题的。

sentences.en: Just bring me a glass of unboiled water.
sentences.zh: 就给我拿杯生水吧。

sentences.en: You can probably guess what's coming.
sentences.zh: 你大概能猜到接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: The next day, he complains of feeling unwell.
sentences.zh: 第二天，他抱怨说感觉不舒服。

sentences.en: He says, don't call a doctor.
sentences.zh: 他说，别叫医生。

sentences.en: I'm sure it'll be fine.
sentences.zh: 我相信会没事的。

sentences.en: Three days later, by the time they do call a doctor, it's obvious it's not fine.
sentences.zh: 三天后，当他们终于叫来医生时，情况显然已经不妙了。

sentences.en: And so it is that at three in the morning, on the 25th of October, 1893,
sentences.zh: 就这样，在1893年10月25日凌晨三点，

sentences.en: Piotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky died of kidney failure.
sentences.zh: 彼得·伊里奇·柴可夫斯基死于肾衰竭。
zh_words: 彼得·伊里奇·柴可夫斯基

sentences.en: Or did he?
sentences.zh: 真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: Because, Dominic, you know I love a mad conspiracy theory.
sentences.zh: 因为多米尼克，你知道我喜欢疯狂的阴谋论。

sentences.en: You do.
sentences.zh: 你确实喜欢。

sentences.en: And it's fair to say that even at the time, there were people who were sceptical of this whole unboiled water story.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，即使在当时，也有人对这整个“生水故事”持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: And they said that Tchaikovsky would never make such a stupid mistake.
sentences.zh: 他们说柴可夫斯基绝不会犯这种愚蠢的错误。

sentences.en: And therefore, there must be a more sinister explanation.
sentences.zh: 因此，一定有更阴险的解释。

sentences.en: And actually, you've said how Mozart was Tchaikovsky's great hero.
sentences.zh: 其实，你之前说过莫扎特是柴可夫斯基的偶像。

sentences.en: There are elements here, aren't there, of the rumours that start to spread around Mozart's death, the possibility that perhaps he'd been murdered.
sentences.zh: 这里面是不是有些关于莫扎特死因的传闻，比如他可能被谋杀了？

sentences.en: And aren't there historians who kind of dabble in these kind of waters about Tchaikovsky?
sentences.zh: 难道没有历史学家在柴可夫斯基的问题上也涉足这些领域吗？

sentences.en: There are indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实有。

sentences.en: As it were.
sentences.zh: 可以说是这样。

sentences.en: Yes, who dabble in these murky waters.
sentences.zh: 是的，那些涉足这些浑水的人。

sentences.en: So a very good example is an eminent British historian, biographer, called David Brown.
sentences.zh: 一个很好的例子是一位杰出的英国历史学家兼传记作家，大卫·布朗。

sentences.en: And he suggested that Tchaikovsky had taken poison, that he'd killed himself, under pressure from his old schoolmates.
sentences.zh: 他认为柴可夫斯基是服毒自杀的，是在他老同学的压力下被迫自尽的。

sentences.en: He said basically his schoolmates had convened this court of honour, and they had handed down their verdict that Tchaikovsky must either take the decent way out,
sentences.zh: 他说基本上他的老同学召集了一个“荣誉法庭”，并判决柴可夫斯基要么选择体面的了断，

sentences.en: or they would expose the secrets of his sex life.
sentences.zh: 要么他们就会曝光他私生活的秘密。

sentences.en: And what credibility do you give to this theory?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这个理论有多少可信度？

sentences.en: You know my methods, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你知道我的方法，汤姆。

sentences.en: I find this very unconvincing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常不可信。

sentences.en: You see, first of all, Tchaikovsky doesn't strike me as a man who is haunted by guilt or anxiety or fear in the autumn of 1893.
sentences.zh: 你看，首先，1893年秋天的柴可夫斯基给我的感觉并不是一个被内疚、焦虑或恐惧所困扰的人。

sentences.en: Actually, he's on cloud nine.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他正处于极度兴奋的状态。

sentences.en: He's just finished his sixth symphony.
sentences.zh: 他刚刚完成了第六交响曲。

sentences.en: He's in very good form.
sentences.zh: 他的状态非常好。

sentences.en: Actually, I think behind all this, people struggle with, I think, the idea that a superstar, an international celebrity of this kind, an artist,
sentences.zh: 其实我认为，人们之所以纠结于此，是因为他们难以接受这样一个事实：像他这样的超级巨星、国际名流、艺术家，

sentences.en: could be cut down by something so random and so meaningless and banal.
sentences.zh: 竟然会被一件如此随机、毫无意义且平庸的事情夺去生命。

sentences.en: And I think people also struggled at the time, especially with the idea that cholera, which was a disease that afflicted the kind of urban poor,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为当时的人们也难以接受霍乱这种折磨城市贫民、

sentences.en: the starving masses, could have carried off such a great man.
sentences.zh: 饥饿大众的疾病，竟然带走了一位如此伟大的人物。

sentences.en: I think they found that very hard to reconcile.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们很难调和这种认知。

sentences.en: Now, for me, I think probably he did have cholera.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，我觉得他很可能确实是得了霍乱。

sentences.en: I think the boiled water story, as bizarre as it is, is probably true.
sentences.zh: 我认为那个关于开水的故事，尽管听起来很离奇，但很可能是真的。

sentences.en: Anyway, what we do know is that his funeral was a massive deal.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我们所知道的是，他的葬礼规模非常宏大。

sentences.en: It was the first commonest funeral ever to be held at the Kazan Cathedral in St. Petersburg.
sentences.zh: 这是圣彼得堡喀山大教堂有史以来举行的第一次公葬。

sentences.en: And it's a sign of his celebrity and his importance that 60,000 people applied for tickets.
sentences.zh: 有6万人申请门票，这足以证明他的名气和重要性。

sentences.en: So that's Tchaikovsky not just dead, but now buried.
sentences.zh: 所以，柴可夫斯基不仅去世了，而且现在已经下葬了。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: And Dominic, I wonder, can you give us your verdict on Tchaikovsky?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我想知道，你能对柴可夫斯基做一个评价吗？

sentences.en: Where does he stand in the history of music?
sentences.zh: 他在音乐史上处于什么地位？

sentences.en: So, a lot of people would see him...
sentences.zh: 很多人会认为他……

sentences.en: Well, he's undoubtedly Russia's most beloved composer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他无疑是俄罗斯最受爱戴的作曲家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think there's a very good argument that he's Russia's greatest composer.
sentences.zh: 我认为有充分的理由说他是俄罗斯最伟大的作曲家。

sentences.en: There have always been critics who have dismissed him as a bit lightweight or a bit easy, as a bit too audience-friendly.
sentences.zh: 一直有评论家认为他有点肤浅，或者说太容易被大众接受了。

sentences.en: I don't think that's a bad thing, by the way, being audience-friendly.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我觉得被大众接受并不是坏事。

sentences.en: I know you don't, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 我知道你不会这么想，多米尼克。

sentences.en: The comparison with Mozart, I think, is a good one.
sentences.zh: 我认为与莫扎特的比较很恰当。

sentences.en: I think nobody since Mozart could do so many different things so quickly and so skillfully.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自莫扎特以来，没有人能如此迅速且熟练地驾驭这么多不同的风格。

sentences.en: And more broadly, Tchaikovsky has come to represent the idea, the musical idea of a Russian soul.
sentences.zh: 更广泛地说，柴可夫斯基已经成为“俄罗斯灵魂”这一音乐理念的代表。

sentences.en: The idea of Russia itself, sort of torn between Europe and Asia, East and West, all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯本身那种在欧洲与亚洲、东方与西方之间挣扎的理念，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And he would have loved that, wouldn't he?
sentences.zh: 他一定会喜欢这个评价的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because he was a massive patriot.
sentences.zh: 因为他是一个彻头彻尾的爱国者。

sentences.en: His country meant so much to him.
sentences.zh: 他的祖国对他意义重大。

sentences.en: What was the thing he was saying about...
sentences.zh: 他当时是怎么说的来着……

sentences.en: He said that, I've never come across anyone who loved Mother Russia more than I did.
sentences.zh: 他说，我从未见过比我更爱俄罗斯母亲的人。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: So, basically, he is to Russia what you are to Britain.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，他之于俄罗斯，就像你之于英国一样。

sentences.en: Oh, Tom.
sentences.zh: 噢，汤姆。

sentences.en: Love it.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And this is the work that really captures, I think, his Russian patriotism.
sentences.zh: 而这部作品，我认为真正捕捉到了他的俄罗斯爱国主义精神。

sentences.en: And it was commissioned in 1880 for the opening of the Cathedral of Christ the Saviour in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 它是在1880年为莫斯科救世主大教堂的落成而委托创作的。

sentences.en: And this cathedral had been commissioned years before, hadn't it?
sentences.zh: 这座大教堂是几年前就委托建造的，对吧？

sentences.en: And it was designed to serve as a memorial to the sacrifices made by the Russian people in their defeat of the invasion by Napoleon, which had happened in 1812.
sentences.zh: 它的设计初衷是为了纪念俄罗斯人民在击败拿破仑入侵（发生在1812年）中所做出的牺牲。

sentences.en: Napoleon had occupied Moscow but had been defeated by the Russian strategy and by the winter and had been forced to retreat in terrible circumstances,
sentences.zh: 拿破仑占领了莫斯科，但被俄罗斯的战略和严冬击败，被迫在极其恶劣的情况下撤退，
